clue.text: Appear absorbing for an announcer

indicators.note: one word absorbing another takes it into its middle, so the first piece holds the second

parts.note: to appear is to come into view
per means for, as in 'per head'

explanation.surface: Someone shows up taking on the job of announcing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appear' looks like the definition, but the announcer comes at the end; 'absorbing' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A compere is the host who introduces acts on a stage or broadcast, an announcer in that sense.

clue.text: Players speed to make ineffective tackle

parts.note: the players in a show are its cast
rate is a word for speed, as in 'at a rate of knots'

explanation.surface: Fast actors set out to neutralise an opposing tackle on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tackle' looks like a sporting challenge, but here it is British slang for a man's genitals.
explanation.definitionFit: To castrate is to remove the testicles, leaving that equipment unable to function: a jokey paraphrase.

clue.text: Locks principal in reception

indicators.note: reception is what a listener hears, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: principal means main, chief

explanation.surface: Hair is the chief thing on show at the welcome desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reception' suggests a front desk, but it means hearing: MAIN sounds like MANE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mane is a long growth of hair, and locks are hair too.

clue.text: Exquisite present wrapped up by midnight?

indicators.note: a thing wrapped by another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: midnight is late at night; the question mark admits the loose equation
present means here, as in answering a roll call

explanation.surface: A delicate gift is wrapped as the clock strikes twelve.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the time word backwards; 'wrapped' signals the container and 'by' is a link. The question mark admits that midnight is only loosely 'late'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means delicate and light, almost unearthly, close to exquisite.

clue.text: Settle on death that hurts!

parts.note: death is the end of life
ow is the cry of pain

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to pass on, and it is painful.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow someone is to settle money or property on them, so the phrases are synonyms.

clue.text: Cut from ear to ear?

indicators.note: said to the ear, the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: an ear is a sensor, an organ detecting sound

explanation.surface: A grisly slash across someone's face, ear to ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from ear to ear' suggests a throat slit, but the first ear is a SENSOR, which sounds like CENSOR; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To censor a text or film is to cut objectionable parts from it.

clue.text: Push member for right to duty-free

indicators.note: one thing put for another replaces it, so a letter is swapped out

parts.note: to exert oneself is to push hard
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP lobbies for the right to buy without paying tax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member for right' puts MP for R in EXERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Exempt means free from an obligation; with duty a tax, duty-free fits.

clue.text: Boss at 10 even provides accommodation

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a raised knob on a surface
10 looks like the letters I and O
even means level, flat

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister at Number 10 kindly puts people up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss at 10' suggests the PM at Downing Street, but a boss is an ornamental STUD; 'at' and 'provides' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio flat is a one-room dwelling, a kind of accommodation.

clue.text: Horses paid out scores

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Bets on horses pay off many times over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges HORSES PAID.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhapsodies are free-form musical compositions, and scores are written music.

clue.text: Use hands to build light shelter

indicators.note: building from parts means putting these letters together in a new order

explanation.surface: Get to work with your hands making a flimsy hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to build' rearranges USE HANDS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade is a canopy or parasol sheltering one from light.

clue.text: Live worm's a source of fine fare

parts.note: to be is to live, exist
a lug is a lugworm, used as bait

explanation.surface: A living worm is put forward as a delicacy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of fine fare' suggests a restaurant, but it is the fish whose roe makes caviar.
explanation.definitionFit: The beluga sturgeon yields the most prized caviar, a luxury food.

clue.text: Sick at work?

parts.note: in means at, as in 'in the office'
a firm is a business where one works

explanation.surface: Is one ill in the office?
explanation.walkthrough: IN FIRM reads 'at the company', so the clue sounds like taking a sick day at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Infirm means weak or ailing, close to sick.

clue.text: Early problems due to power splitting tiny particles

indicators.note: a thing splitting another breaks into its middle, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: grains are tiny particles of sand or salt
owing means due, of a debt

explanation.surface: A physics paper on atom-splitting has its teething troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tiny particles' suggests atoms being split, but they are sand-type particles; 'splitting' signals the container and 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing pains are difficulties in the early stage of an enterprise, figuratively.

clue.text: Instrument with glass sheet protecting hot film

parts.note: the cello is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: a thing protecting another surrounds it, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a pane is a sheet of window glass
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A musician's case with a glass panel shielding a heated reel of movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' suggests a movie, but it is a thin transparent wrap; 'protecting' puts H inside PANE; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cellophane is a thin transparent wrapping film.

clue.text: One finding ways to capture class soldier?

definitions.text: One finding ways to capture class soldier?

indicators.note: capturing something takes it inside, so these pieces go within the others

parts.note: ways are streets, two of them ST and ST
rate is class, as in first-rate
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A military planner works out how to take a top-class trooper prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'ways' gives two street abbreviations, one either side; 'to capture' signals the container and 'One finding' is a link in the wordplay reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A planner who devises methods of achieving goals, including capturing enemy troops, is a strategist.

clue.text: Kindly release outspoken oriental kids?

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the phrase gives the answer by sound

parts.note: youngsters in the Orient are youth in Asia

explanation.surface: A merciful liberation for Eastern children, put bluntly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kindly release' is a gentle phrase for mercy killing.
explanation.definitionFit: Euthanasia is ending a life to spare suffering, a merciful release from pain.

clue.text: Octave's arranged for bird

indicators.note: arranged means set in a new order, as music is arranged

parts.note: octave read as written, the 's meaning 'is'

explanation.surface: A musical interval is scored for a birdsong part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges OCTAVE; the 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a wading bird with an upturned bill.

clue.text: See 19
Pure lack of time when continent's in upheaval

indicators.note: something in upheaval is thrown into disorder, so its letters are rearranged
a lack of something means it is missing, so this letter is taken away from the pool

parts.note: continent read as written; the 's is not a letter

explanation.surface: A clean slate is lacking time while a landmass is in turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lack of' says T is taken out of CONTINENT, and 'in upheaval' rearranges what is left; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocent means free from guilt or corruption, morally pure.

clue.text: Went quickly through sheets of metal containing iron

indicators.note: a word containing another holds it inside

parts.note: lead is a heavy metal
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Something sped through iron-rich sheets of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheets' looks like metal plate but belongs to the definition, the pages of a book; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have leafed through papers is to have turned their pages quickly.

clue.text: Audience of public gallery make observations

indicators.note: an audience hears, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: common means public, shared by all
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Spectators at a public gallery remark on what they see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audience of' says the word for public is taken by its sound, a loose homophone; the Tate is a group of British national art galleries.
explanation.definitionFit: To commentate is to give a running commentary, making remarks on events as they happen.

clue.text: Offered up nut to great ape

indicators.note: in a down clue, offered up means the whole run is lifted and read backwards

parts.note: nob is slang for the head, also a nut
big means great

explanation.surface: A nut is held up for a large primate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great ape' looks like one phrase, but 'great' is wordplay; 'Offered up' turns the whole run round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A gibbon is a small ape of South-East Asia.

clue.text: Penchant of French for the penetrating prognosis

indicators.note: a thing penetrating another enters it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a prognosis is a prediction of an illness's course
le is the French word for the

explanation.surface: A doctor's liking for an incisive forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penetrating' signals the container and 'of' is a link; a prognosis is a doctor's forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: A predilection is a liking or preference, the same as a penchant.

clue.text: Set up ball to include women's stuff

indicators.note: including a thing means taking it inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: in golf a ball set on a peg is teed
W is the abbreviation for women

explanation.surface: A golfer prepares a shot that takes the ladies into account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuff' is cloth, a material; 'to include' puts W inside TEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a rough woollen cloth, and stuff is an old word for woven material.

clue.text: Surprise admission to best university

indicators.note: the letters are admitted inside the words, so the answer is found within them

explanation.surface: Getting into a top university comes as a shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admission to' points inside 'best university'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to astonish, overwhelm with surprise.

clue.text: See 1
Members' position leads to all kept in ministry backing opposition

indicators.note: the leads are the front letters of each following word

explanation.surface: Everyone in government backing the opposition stands with hands on hips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' looks like MPs, but it means limbs: the arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms akimbo are bent with hands on hips, a posture of the limbs.

clue.text: Mendieta's transfer is lunacy

indicators.note: a transfer moves things around, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Gaizka Mendieta, a Spanish footballer, read as written; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A footballer's move between clubs is madness.
explanation.walkthrough: Mendieta's world-record transfer to Lazio in 2001 was thought crazy; 'transfer' rearranges MENDIETA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dementia is mental decline, loosely madness.

clue.text: Surviving when on-board equipment doesn't show south

indicators.note: a letter that doesn't show is left out

parts.note: a sextant is a ship's navigation instrument

explanation.surface: A ship's gear survives even when the southern bearing is missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Extant means still in existence, surviving.

clue.text: Big thaw causes river to swamp shelter

indicators.note: swamping something floods over it, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a tent is a shelter

explanation.surface: Melting snow makes a river flood a camping spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big thaw' suggests melting ice, but it is easing of political tension; 'causes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Détente is an easing of hostility between nations, a thaw in relations.
